output.text:
# Reading list on OAuth

The best single explainer is the IETF overview at https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749 and the PKCE extension at https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636.

A diagram of the flow: ![flow](https://example.com/oauth-flow.png)

Key points: tokens are short-lived; refresh tokens must be stored safely; PKCE binds the authorization code to the client that asked for it.

This is a concise reading list on OAuth for developers and security practitioners.  

- The IETF RFC 6749 (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749) is the best single explainer of OAuth 2.0.  
- The PKCE extension is defined in RFC 7636 (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636).  
- A diagram illustrating the OAuth flow is provided (though the image link is illustrative).  
- OAuth tokens are short-lived.  
- Refresh tokens must be stored safely.  
- PKCE binds the authorization code to the client that requested it.
